Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Card Reference 3 Gameplay 4 Scoring 5 Game End Objective Collect the most points by winning Clashes against your opponents. The game ends after 3 Bouts or when a player reaches 200 points. Card Reference Number Cards (2–13): Used to meet or exceed the value of the active Clash Card. Star Cards: Wildcards that automatically beat any number card. If two Stars are played, they result in a tie. Gameplay A Bout consists of 5 Clashes for a stack of cards. All players act simultaneously. Setup: Each player draws 5 cards from their own deck. The Clash: The top card of a 5-card Clash stack is revealed. Each player chooses one of their 5 hand cards and places it face-down. All cards are revealed simultaneously. Determining the Winner: Your card must be at least equal to the value of the revealed Clash Card to be eligible. Among eligible players, the highest card wins. The winner takes the Clash Card and all player cards played this round into their Point Pile. Ties & Misses: If no one meets the Clash Card value or the highest cards played are tied, there is no winner. All cards remain in the pot to be won in the next Clash. Next Clash: Reveal the next card from the stack until all 5 hand cards have been played. Scoring At the end of each Bout, players count their Point Piles: 5 points: Each card with a value of 10 or more. 10 points: Each Star Card. 15 point bonus: Awarded to the player with the most cards in their Point Pile. Game End The game ends after 3 Bouts or once a player hits 200 points. The player with the highest score wins. In this innovative reimagining of the classic game War, players clash against their opponents across five stacks — no matter the player count!

Fight Five is an elemental tug-of-war. In each of the five rounds, players will draw five cards and challenge their opponents for control of five different stacks. Win the clash and take the cards for endgame scoring! Did you tie? Then that stack only grows bigger (and more valuable) for the next clash.

Clever play across all five stacks will win the day, and watch out for Star Clash Cards that will beat out all other cards! 
 Be the first to 200 points, or have the most points after three bouts of five rounds.

[Rating: 2/10] It is basically multi player War but you fight multiple  wars all at once and with 1 card each war. Not for me.

[Rating: 3/10] Fancy version of war, didn't think I'd like it while it was being explained to me, and I was right. Meh.

[Rating: 4/10] This wasn't very much fun.  The different element decks are all the same, and the gameplay really felt dull.  The biggest problem for me is that you always draw and play 5 cards, yet only higher cards are worth any points.  This makes it so that your best cards may come out in a round where they are worthless, yet you are forced to play them immediately.  However, in addition to that, the game just has no real feeling of joy or purpose. [Rating: 4/10] Number card "royal battle" to try grab most high cards. There is not anything much to it.

[Rating: 5/10] A trick taking game where you play against all players all at once. All players will play a card in each line facing all opponents (middle is played against all players). The winner of the trick is the player with the highest value if its higher than the reward card. Star cards are an auto win, unless another star is played. The winner will take the reward card, and all cards into that lane. In a tie or the reward card is higher than the cards played, no winner is declared.
